subject.title: Bug: messaging tool suppress mechanism skips when tool fails then retries in same turn, causing duplicate delivery

question: Should same-route assistant text that matches an in-flight `message(action=send)` retry be held and released by default if the pending send never confirms, using full route plus content as the match key?
rationale: The source proves the timing gap, but choosing pending-as-sent versus hold-and-release changes user-visible fallback behavior and can trade duplicate messages for silent drops.

options.title: Hold and release by default
options.body: Hold matching replies while a same-route send is pending, drop them only after confirmed delivery, and release them if the pending send fails or never resolves.

options.title: Suppress against pending sends
options.body: Treat pending sends as delivered for suppression, which reduces duplicates but can leave the user with no response after failed or abandoned retries.

options.title: Keep committed-only suppression
options.body: Preserve the current fallback guarantee and accept duplicate delivery during retry timing windows until a broader delivery policy changes.

recommendation.title: Hold and release by default
recommendation.body: Hold matching replies while a same-route send is pending, drop them only after confirmed delivery, and release them if the pending send fails or never resolves.

likelyOwner.reason: This decision sits in the embedded handler and reply-dedupe policy surface where steipete has the strongest recent feature-history trail.
